physical_harm: Injuries including incised wounds on legs, fractured hands, and internal injuries leading to death
number_of_offences: Three offences/counts charged, two finally upheld
motive: Alleged motive of caste-based discrimination (calling the victim 'Chamar')
key_evidence_accepted: The FIR was rightly relied upon by the courts below as dying declaration of the victim-deceased. The testimony of PW1 (wife of deceased) and PW2 (sister-in-law of the deceased) disclosed that the appellants opened an assault on the victim which led to his death. The recoveries of the weapons in question viz., lathi, sword and axe also lend sufficient corroboration to the prosecution’s case.
witness_credibility: The substantive testimony of both PW1 and PW2 clearly discloses that the appellants had opened an assault on the victim which led to his death. The assertion on part of PW1 that her earlier statement recorded during investigation was read over to her does not mean that she was tutored to follow the line of prosecution. No such questions were put to PW2. Thus, even if the testimony of PW1 is eschewed from consideration, the deposition of PW2 along with the dying declaration of the victim completely clinch the matter against the appellants.
post_offence_conduct: Devilal and Gokul were released on bail by this Court vide Order dated 08.04.2009, they are directed to surrender before the concerned Police Station within two weeks from today, failing which the bail bonds furnished at the time of their release on bail shall stand forfeited and they shall immediately be arrested by the concerned police to undergo the sentence imposed upon them.
bail_history: Devilal and Gokul were released on bail by this Court vide Order dated 08.04.2009
trial_duration: The incident occurred in July, 1998. The trial judgment was dated 01.05.1999. The High Court decision was dated 14.09.2006. The Supreme Court decision was on 25 February 2021.
legal_representation: Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned Senior Advocate for the appellants and Mr. Harmeet Singh Ruprah, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent-State
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence affirmed. High Court: Conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: Conviction and sentence affirmed for Devilal and Gokul; sentence set aside for Amrat Ram, matter remitted to Juvenile Justice Board.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution relied upon the FIR as a dying declaration of the victim-deceased, the presence of PW1 and PW2, their testimony about the assault leading to the victim's death, and the recovery of weapons (lathi, sword, and axe) as corroboration of the case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the FIR could not be relied upon as the deceased could not have made a statement to the police due to medical evidence suggesting unconsciousness, and that the witnesses were tutored, thereby undermining their testimony.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the legal principle that the determination of juvenility under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, should be based on the age of the accused at the time of the commission of the offence, even if they became adults after the Act came into force.
precedent_relied_upon: Mumtaz alias Muntyaz vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2016) 11 SCC 786; Satya Deo alias Bhoorey vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2020) 10 SCC 555; Jitendra Singh vs. State of U.P (2013) 11 SCC 193
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the conviction that the appellants were guilty of the offence, with the exception of the third appellant 'AR', who was deemed a juvenile under the 2000 Act and thus the life imprisonment was set aside.
other_sentence_order: The matter relating to 'AR' was remitted to the Juvenile Justice Board for determining the appropriate quantum of fine. Devilal and Gokul were directed to surrender to the police within two weeks or face forfeiture of bail bonds.
